item.title: NYSC kidnapping: Identities of suspects vindicate us – IPOB
item.description: …Raise questions over profiling of Igbo youths …Group demands investigation into alleged sponsors of insecurity in South-East By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has called for a thorough investigation into the abduction of prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members along the Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State, following the arraignment of five suspects over the incident. The group said the suspects’ identities raised questions about the attribution of kidnappings and other criminal activities in the South-East to its members and the Eastern Security Network (ESN) before investigations establish those responsible. The suspects were identified as Usman Aliyu, Babangida Aliyu, Mohammed Ali, Aminu Haliru and Ibrahim Jiji. In a statement issued on Tuesday by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Comrade Emma Powerful, IPOB said the case reinforced its longstanding position that its members and ESN had been wrongly blamed for insecurity in the region. The group argued that, had the suspects not been apprehended, Igbo youths and ESN members might have been accused of the crime, potentially exposing innocent people to arrest and other alleged mistreatment. “Had this atrocious kidnapping happened without these suspects being caught, who would the Nigerian security apparatus and hostile media have blamed?” IPOB asked. The group said previous incidents in the South-East had similarly been attributed to IPOB and ESN, insisting that criminal allegations should be subjected to evidence-based investigations. IPOB maintained that its members were not responsible for kidnappings in the region, adding that ESN was established to protect communities, farmers and residents against armed attacks. The group commended the Director of the Department of State Services (DSS) in Imo State and the prosecuting team, describing the case as an opportunity to establish the facts surrounding the abduction. It called for a comprehensive investigation into the suspects’ identities, origins, networks and alleged accomplices, urging authorities to make the findings public in accordance with the law. IPOB also urged security agencies to investigate criminal activities based on evidence rather than ethnicity, political affiliation or unverified allegations. The statement renewed the group’s criticism of the continued detention of its leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, arguing that his warnings about security threats in the region had not received adequate attention. IPOB further called on South-East governors and political leaders to strengthen security in rural communities and forests, protect lives and property, and ensure that innocent residents were not unfairly associated with criminal activities. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC described the remark as a damning assessment of the ruling party’s security record, coming from a senior figure charged with promoting Tinubu’s re-election. Yari was quoted as saying: “If Buhari, who is a retired military man, could not wipe out insecurity, what can Tinubu do?” The ADC-PCC said the comment reflected a failure of confidence in the APC’s ability to address a crisis that has left communities vulnerable to banditry, terrorism, kidnapping and killings. “For a party that has been in power for nearly 12 years, this is a shocking admission of failure. item.title: Dele Giwa: NGE demands justice 40 years after murder
item.description: The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has called on relevant authorities to revisit the unresolved assassination of renowned journalist, Dele Giwa, insisting that the passage of 40 years must not extinguish the quest for justice. Giwa, co-founder of Newswatch magazine, was killed by a parcel bomb delivered to his home on October 19, 1986. Four decades after the incident, no one has been brought to justice for his murder. In a statement on Monday to mark the 40th anniversary of Giwa’s assassination, the NGE President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh, described the unresolved case as a painful test of Nigeria’s commitment to press freedom, public accountability and the rule of law. The Guild said the country could not afford to allow the case to disappear into history, stressing that the responsibility to investigate serious crimes did not expire with time or changes in government. “Forty years is a long time to wait for justice. It is an unconscionably long time for a nation that claims to uphold the rule of law,” the Guild said. It urged the appropriate authorities to revisit the case, examine credible evidence that might still be available, preserve relevant records and pursue every lawful avenue towards establishing the truth about Giwa’s death. The Guild, however, cautioned against trial by media, insisting that its demand was for a credible investigation rather than the condemnation of anyone without evidence. “We are not calling for trial by media. We are not asking anyone to be condemned without evidence. We are demanding that a grave crime against a Nigerian citizen, a distinguished journalist and the freedom of the press should not remain an enduring symbol of impunity,” it said. The NGE made the call as it highlighted the significance of a book, Dele Giwa’s Granite Journalism, unveiled on Monday to preserve the late journalist’s professional legacy. The NGE made the call as it highlighted the significance of a book, Dele Giwa’s Granite Journalism, unveiled on Monday to preserve the late journalist’s professional legacy. The Guild expressed concern that the unresolved murder could send a troubling message to journalists investigating corruption, probing abuses of power or exposing the activities of influential interests. It asked whether the passage of time, the death of witnesses or changes in government should diminish the state’s obligation to pursue justice, insisting that the answer must be no. “An unresolved murder is not a closed chapter. It is an open wound in the nation’s conscience,” it said. Beyond the demand for justice, the NGE urged contemporary journalists and editors to reflect on the state of the profession, particularly its independence from political and commercial interests. It said the principles represented by Giwa required journalists to demonstrate courage, accuracy, independence, fairness and a commitment to the truth. “Courage without accuracy can become recklessness; independence without ethics can become irresponsibility,” the Guild said, adding that journalism worth defending must be both fearless and scrupulous, independent and accountable. It further warned against reducing Giwa’s memory to annual commemorations without concrete efforts to address the circumstances of his death. “Remembrance without action risks becoming an elaborate way of accommodating injustice,” it said. The Guild called for Giwa’s professional ideals to be taught in journalism schools, discussed in newsrooms and preserved in the national historical record, urging younger journalists to appreciate the sacrifices made by earlier generations in defending press freedom. It added that the defence of press freedom was not the exclusive responsibility of journalists, noting that attacks on media practitioners also threatened citizens’ right to reliable information. item.title: Oyo fixes Dec 29 for council polls
item.description: …approves N13.49bn for LAUTECH annex By Adeola Badru Oyo State Government has fixed December 29, 2026, for chairmanship and councillorship elections across the state’s 33 local government areas, while approving billions of naira in funding for electoral preparations, nursing education and healthcare infrastructure. The Commissioner for Information, Mr. Dotun Oyelade, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday following the State Executive Council meeting, which approved the release of the government’s counterpart funding to the Oyo State Independent Electoral Commission (OYSIEC) to commence preparations for the local government elections. According to the statement, the elections will be jointly funded by the state government and the 33 local government councils, with the councils contributing 60 per cent of the total cost and the state providing the remaining 40 per cent. The local government councils are expected to contribute N2,566,800,000, while the state government will provide N1,711,200,000, bringing the total funding for the elections to N4,278,000,000. The statement said the Executive Council had approved the counterpart funding to ensure that OYSIEC could begin preparations for the polls scheduled for December 29. In another major decision, the council approved N437,446,398.58 for the accreditation requirements of the Nursing Programme at Abiola Ajimobi Technical University, as the institution seeks to expand its academic offerings beyond science and technology. Explaining the rationale for the funding, Oyelade said the intervention would support the university’s diversification strategy and strengthen its capacity to operate sustainably. item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich could be without manager Vincent Kompany, goalkeeper Manuel Neuer and midfielder Joshua Kimmich for Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Arsenal, assistant coach Aaron Danks has said. Neuer has returned to training over the past two days, but Bayern are yet to decide whether the goalkeeper will be available for the Arsenal encounter. Kimmich’s participation also remains uncertain. However, the German champions head into the encounter with confidence after thrashing RB Leipzig 6-1 in the Bundesliga on Saturday. item.title: Plateau Assembly Adopts State Police Bill, Backs Decentralised Policing
item.description: The Plateau State House of Assembly has adopted the recommendations of its Ad-hoc Committee in support of the proposed constitutional amendment to establish State Police in Nigeria. The decision was reached during Monday’s plenary session presided over by the Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, following the presentation and consideration of the committee’s report. item.title: Seven-Up Bottling Company Confirms Authenticity of Yellow Covers as Part of an Exciting Initiative
item.description: Seven-Up Bottling Company (SBC) has sparked curiosity among consumers with the appearance of bright yellow covers on plastic bottles of key brands, including Pepsi, Mirinda, 7UP, Teem, and Supa Komando. The yellow covers are authentic packaging as a temporary feature in an upcoming initiative the company says will bring something exciting to consumers like never before in selected regions. Seven-Up Bottling Company (SBC) began building anticipation through a teaser communication alluding to the distinctive yellow covers appearing on bottles in retail outlets, prompting questions about what is coming next. An Instagram post on Pepsi’s Instagram page reinforced the intrigue, promising consumers that “Something exciting is Coming.” The message appears to resonate with consumers, judging by reactions to its social media post. Comments range from expressions of excitement to playful encouragement, with users eager to see what the beverage company has planned. “Let’s gooooo ,” commented verified Instagram user the_obinnan, while eromz.thecreator described the development as “Too activeeeee my favorite drinkkkkkkk.” Another user, mustapha_shi2, added, “Bring it on .” The reactions suggest that the yellow covers have become more than a packaging change in the eyes of consumers. They have become clues in a developing brand mystery, encouraging people to watch for the next announcement and speculate about what the company has in store. While Seven-up Bottling Company has yet to disclose the details of the upcoming initiative, its teaser messaging suggests that the yellow covers are part of a wider campaign designed to build excitement ahead of the reveal. For now, consumers are left watching, guessing and waiting to find out what lies behind the bright yellow covers. item.title: Death toll from Houthi strike on Yemen govt camp rises to 73
item.description: Local Yemeni authorities on Tuesday raised the death toll from a Houthi strike a day earlier on a military camp belonging to government forces to 73, as fighting between the foes escalates. It marked the deadliest attack in weeks as fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Yemen’s internationally recognised, Saudi-supported government rages after the collapse of a years-long truce. The death toll from Monday’s strike on the camp in the energy-rich Shabwa province “increased to 73 martyrs, while search and follow-up efforts are ongoing to discover the fate of 14 missing people”, provincial authorities said in a statement. Local authorities had put the death toll at 53 on Monday, adding that more than 200 others were injured, all new members of the internal security forces who were undergoing training. Majed al-Nuzaili, spokesperson for the Yemeni armed forces, stated Monday on X that the Houthis targeted Shabwa with three ballistic missiles, and that the attack “struck a training center for personnel of security and police agencies.” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree later confirmed that the group was responsible for the attack, saying it targeted “Saudi enemy gatherings in Al-Alam camp, which is run by a Saudi officer from the eastern regions”. Shabwa contains major oil and gas fields and is home to the Balhaf liquefied natural gas terminal, the country’s largest energy facility and a key economic asset. A government military source in the province on Monday said the army feared the strikes could pave the way for a ground offensive “similar to what happened in Mokha”, the strategic Red Sea port city seized by the Houthis last month. item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has begun moves to establish a regulatory framework for nutrition practice in Nigeria, with lawmakers and stakeholders meeting on Tuesday to consider a bill seeking to establish the Nutritionists Registration Council of Nigeria. The proposed legislation is aimed at strengthening professional standards, improving the quality of nutrition services and protecting Nigerians from harmful or misleading nutritional advice. Declaring the public hearing open, Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, said the establishment of a Standing Committee on Nutrition and Food Security reflected the importance of nutrition to public health, education, healthcare expenditure and national productivity. item.title: Lekki shooting: ‘Why didn’t you ask Buhari?’ Tinubu’s aide faults Atiku’s EndSARS question
item.description: President Bola Tinubu’s Special Assistant on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, has faulted former Vice President Atiku Abubakar for demanding accountability over the October 2020 Lekki Toll Gate shooting, asking why he did not raise the issue during his visits to former President Muhammadu Buhari. Olusegun accused Atiku of exploiting the sixth anniversary of the #EndSARS protests to advance his presidential ambition, arguing that the former vice president had opportunities to question Buhari, who was president when the shooting occurred. In a statement responding to Atiku’s call for answers, the presidential aide recalled that the former vice president visited Buhari in Daura, Katsina State, on June 22, 2024, and again at his retirement residence in Kaduna on April 11, 2025. “Those two opportunities presented you with chances to ask former President Buhari, who was President at the time of the Lekki Toll Gate protests, the questions you are now asking President Tinubu,” Olusegun said.
